+title: HubModelLoader detects the model format from a local path
+---
+The agent config must accept a local path as a model reference and find the format by itself: a .mlpackage folder is CoreML, safetensors files are MLX. HubModelFormat.detect works on the files of a Hub repository only. HubModelLoader.format(of:) looks in the Hub cache or asks the Hub. Add a local-path branch: when the reference is an existing directory, list its top-level names and call HubModelFormat.detect. Make MLXModelLoader and CoreMLModelLoader load from that directory with no download. Add tests for a CoreML folder, an MLX folder, and a folder with both. Router ModelRef must accept the path too; that is a separate Router card.
\ No newline at end of file

+## Review Findings (2026-11-01 10:26)
+
+> Scope: `review sha HEAD~1..HEAD` — reviewed the diffs only — lines this change added or modified. 7 file(s) reviewed, 5 not reviewed.

+> 4 file(s) not reviewed — excluded by an ignore rule:

+
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/ModelPool/CoreMLModelLoader.swift:149` `reuse/reuse` — footprintBytes resolves a local folder or a cache snapshot with its own expression. MLXModelLoader already has the same resolution in snapshotDirectory(of:), which checks localDirectory first and then the cache. Two loaders now hold the same rule, so a change to one (for example to the error or the revision handling) will not reach the other. Move the local-or-cache resolution to one shared place, such as a method on HubSource that takes a ModelRef and a revision and returns the folder or nil. Have both MLXModelLoader.snapshotDirectory and CoreMLModelLoader.footprintBytes call it, and keep each loader's own error type at its call site.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/ModelPool/CoreMLPackage.swift:160` `completeness/invariant-propagation` — The compiled-model key for a local package changes only when Manifest.json changes. The doc comment says a package that changes in place compiles again, but a change to the weight files without a manifest change keeps the old compiled model. The stated guarantee is wider than the code. Either include the modification dates or sizes of the weight files in `localRevision`, or narrow the doc comment and the change description so they say only a manifest change triggers a new compile. Add a test that changes a weight file in place and checks that the revision changes.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/ModelPool/CoreMLPackage.swift:162` `swift/preconditions` — The manifest date read uses `try?` and falls back to `.distantPast` with no `assertionFailure` and no log. If the manifest cannot be read, every later state of the package gets the same revision string, so a package that changes in place is not compiled again. This is the defect the change exists to prevent, and the failure is silent. When the read fails, call `assertionFailure` and write a log line that names the manifest path, then keep the fallback. Alternatively, make `localRevision` throw a typed error and let `CoreMLModelLoader` report it.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/ModelPool/HubModelLoader.swift:175` `reuse/reuse` — The new local-folder branch in format(of:) repeats the snapshot branch below it (contentsOfDirectory, then HubModelFormat.detect(paths:)). Two copies of the same folder-to-format step can diverge. The local branch also omits the non-empty check and the try? handling that the snapshot branch uses, so the two paths already differ. Resolve one folder first, then run the listing and detect once. For example: let folder = key.ref.localDirectory ?? hub.snapshotDirectory(of:revision:); if let folder, let names = try? contentsOfDirectory(...), !names.isEmpty { return detect(names) }. Decide in one place whether an empty or unreadable local folder should throw.
